- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days), then underestimates later.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 82.21 → 84.99, 83.26 → 86.37), then fails to correct downward.
- Underestimates mean-reverting periods — model holds too high a mean, fails to adjust toward historical averages.
- Forecasts lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in downward trends.
- Overconfidence in short-term momentum: model assumes trend continues, ignores volatility decay or policy-induced corrections.
- High variance in later forecast days (e.g., 88.96, 95.04) suggests model overreacts to recent spikes without proper smoothing.
- Model underestimates downward corrections after upward moves — fails to recognize policy or market cooling effects.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent peaks — model “clings” to recent highs.
